title: Predicting the Distribution of Treatment Effects: A Covariate-Adjustment Approach
abstract: arXiv:2407.14635v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Important questions for impact evaluation require knowledge not only of average effects, but of the distribution of treatment effects. The inability to observe individual counterfactuals makes answering these empirical questions challenging. I propose an inference approach for points of the distribution of treatment effects that uses predicted counterfactuals through covariate adjustment. I provide finite-sample valid inference using sample-splitting and asymptotically valid inference using cross-fitting under arguably weak conditions. Revisiting five randomized controlled trials on microcredit that reported null average effects, I find important distributional impacts, with some individuals helped and others harmed by the increased credit access.

translated_title: 预测处理效应的分布：一种协变量调整方法
translated_abstract: 影响评估中的重要问题不仅需要了解平均效应，还需要了解处理效应的分布。由于无法观测个体的反事实结果，回答这些实证问题极具挑战性。本文提出了一种针对处理效应分布各分位点的推断方法，该方法通过协变量调整利用预测的反事实结果。在相当弱的条件下，我提供了基于样本分割的有限样本有效推断，以及基于交叉拟合的渐近有效推断。通过重新审视五项报告了零平均效应的小额信贷随机对照试验，我发现存在重要的分布性影响：信贷可得性的提高使一些人受益，而使另一些人受损。
tldr: 本文提出一种通过协变量调整利用预测反事实来推断处理效应分布的新方法，并通过对五项小额信贷随机对照试验的再分析发现，尽管平均效应为零，信贷扩张实际上使部分人受益、部分人受损，存在显著的分布性影响。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes a covariate-adjustment inference approach using predicted counterfactuals to estimate the distribution of treatment effects, and reanalysis of five microcredit RCTs with null average effects reveals significant distributional impacts where some individuals benefit while others are harmed by increased credit access.
